cls: Chlorite-based oxygen-transfer agent / immunomodulator (topical wound-healing agent and investigational IV immunomodulator)

summary: Tetrachlorodecaoxygen anion (commonly tetrachlorodecaoxide, TCDO) is a stabilized chlorite-based oxygen-transfer complex. It is formulated topically as Oxoferin for promotion of wound healing and intravenously as WF10 (Immunokine), an immunomodulatory preparation studied in conditions such as radiation-induced injury (e.g., chronic radiation proctitis/cystitis) and as adjunctive immune modulation. The agent is proposed to act through oxidative/oxygen-transfer effects on macrophages and tissue and to modulate inflammatory and immune responses. It is not FDA-approved, and the supporting clinical evidence is limited and largely regional. Dosing details are not well standardized in widely available sources; where specific data are uncertain this record states 'Not well characterized' rather than asserting unverified figures.

moa: Tetrachlorodecaoxide is a stabilized complex containing chlorite and oxygen species and is described as an oxygen-transfer / oxidative agent. The proposed mechanism involves delivery of reactive oxygen/chlorite species that support oxidative metabolism in macrophages and wound tissue, promoting phagocytic and tissue-repair processes (topical wound healing), and modulating inflammatory and immune cell activity (intravenous immunomodulation). The precise molecular targets and clinical mechanism are not fully established and remain incompletely characterized.
